mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investors shift from cash to equities during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential housing starts (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in household demand, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day returns as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST < 1200 and RSAFS < 520000.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-pandemic recovery phase, a GDP growth rate exceeding 2.0% annualized (computed from quarterly GDPC1 change) indicates accelerating economic activity, generating positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized during the post-pandemic recovery phase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer credit (RSAFS) above $500 billion indicates rising household spending, generating positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as retail and consumer discretionary sectors benefit.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > $500 billion.

mechanism_narrative: An annual inflation rate exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL) signals monetary policy tightening and real interest rate increases, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in manufacturing employment (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 20-day returns as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both PAYEMS < 140000 and INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime, a manufacturing production index (INDPRO) below 95.0 indicates severe industrial contraction, causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as global supply chains face disruption.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 during a supply shock regime.
